source.title: Auditing Asset-Specific Preferences in Financial Large Language Models: Evidence from Bitcoin Representations and Portfolio Allocation

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature search and intervention methods to Gemma 3 LLMs, reporting findings about recoverable features in a real-model setting rather than testing toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own SAE feature-search and cross-scale feature results, which bear on V4, and a wider-dictionary check that bears on V5. Behavioral asset rankings, financial allocation results, and steering outcomes are not evidence about superposition geometry or limited-capacity polysemanticity and are not recorded as rows for those versions. The paper does not measure feature overlap, interference, nearly orthogonal directions, or neuron polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: This is a financial-preference audit. It uses pretrained GemmaScope 2 SAEs as a tool to find one Bitcoin-selective feature, then tests that feature's steering leverage on asset choices and portfolio allocation. It never asks whether features are superposed: no feature-versus-dimension counts, no interference or overlap measures, no neuron polysemanticity, and no assessment of whether the SAE recovers the model's features in general. Finding one concept-selective latent in an off-the-shelf dictionary shows the tool working, not a test of V4 or V5. The single wider-dictionary remark is an unquantified limitation note.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude three further things. Behaviorally, Bitcoin's ranking across nine LLMs is frame-dependent and tracks attribute profiles rather than names. Steering f11887 shifts portfolio allocation by about ±5 pp in bounded, profile-dependent ways. Transcoder graphs show distributed asset representations feeding generic comparison machinery, with no monetary-specific circuit.
record.recipe_differences: This is an LLM interpretability and activation-steering audit using SAE feature search, not the original toy-network feature-over-dimension experiments or their geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering leverage varies by Gemma 3 scale: it is strong in 27B and 1B, intermediate in 4B, and weak in 12B. The study also reports that the feature effect varies across financial frames, but that result is not a test of superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: In all four Gemma 3 sizes a Bitcoin-selective SAE latent is found, but its steering leverage varies widely: 27B and 1B at the 100th percentile, 4B at 80%, 12B at 62% (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation selectivity of SAE latents does not imply causal steering leverage (representation–leverage gap).

fits_no_version.finding: Decomposing a steering vector into SAE features loads almost entirely on dense, always-on features. The Bitcoin-selective feature carries near-zero weight.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decompositions of steering vectors are dominated by dense features and miss content-specific latents.

fits_no_version.finding: Transcoder attribution graphs show asset-specific entity features, distributed across layers, that feed shared comparison machinery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Asset concepts are represented by multiple distributed transcoder features rather than one localized circuit.

record.problems: The representation evidence is limited to one model family. SAE feature basis dependence is acknowledged, and feature steering does not show that the SAE feature is natively recruited. The study does not test feature overlap, interference, superposition geometry, or the capacity account of polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted. Other asset-ranking, pairwise-steering, portfolio-allocation, transcoder, and mechanism-boundary results do not measure the claim versions’ superposition geometry, capacity mechanism, or canonical feature status.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
No study of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no general SAE recovery evaluation; only one concept latent is located per model.
Wider-dictionary similarity is asserted, not quantified; no completeness, stability or canonicity test.

record.verdict_notes: The reader over-linked tool-use results to V4/V5. The paper's SAE results concern one selected concept latent and its steering leverage, not superposition or the canonical status of dictionary features. Cross-scale models are all IT variants. The causal relation between f11887 and the native transcoder features is untested.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network superposition test, feature-over-dimension sweep, sparsity transition, interference measure, or regular geometry analysis.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Tests recovery of sparse SAE features in Gemma 3, but not whether features are spread across many neurons; the representation evidence is limited to one model family.
Reports basis dependence and a wider-dictionary check, but does not establish SAE-feature completeness, canonicality, or stability across broad model and training settings.
Uses single decoder directions for interventions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features or test the dimensionality of the model’s represented features.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 27B IT
rows.operation_detail: Searched 16,384 Layer 16 SAE features for differential activation on Bitcoin-positive prompts versus other categories.
rows.measure: Cohen’s d and category mean activations for the selected feature
rows.baseline: Other categories combined; category means were 0.00 for crypto-general, traditional finance, and non-financial prompts.
rows.value: Cohen’s d = 2.055; Bitcoin-positive mean activation = 28.52; nonzero rate = 0.733.
rows.note: Feature 11887 was reported as the dominant Bitcoin-selective feature in the searched dictionary.
rows.check: Selection value. Cohen's d on the 60-prompt discovery set was used to choose f11887, so it is a feature-selection statistic, not a test of superposition or of SAE feature recovery.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 1B
rows.operation_detail: Differential activation search identified a Bitcoin-selective SAE feature; the study also evaluated its steering effect.
rows.measure: Bitcoin-selective feature identification and pairwise log-probability shift
rows.value: Feature identified as Bitcoin-selective; s150 shift +0.95; percentile 100% among 50 random single-feature controls.
rows.note: The authors report selective features at every tested Gemma 3 scale; steering leverage was strong for this model.
rows.check: The feature was chosen as the highest-d feature over 4 layers, which is a selection value. The reported value is a steering shift, not a superposition measure. Stage is instruct-tuned: Table 15 lists gemma-3-1b-it.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 4B
rows.operation_detail: Differential activation search identified a Bitcoin-selective SAE feature; the study also evaluated its steering effect.
rows.measure: Bitcoin-selective feature identification and pairwise log-probability shift
rows.value: Feature identified as Bitcoin-selective; s150 shift +0.95; percentile 80% among 50 random single-feature controls.
rows.note: The authors describe activation selectivity as reproducible across tested scales, while reporting intermediate steering leverage for this model.
rows.check: Selection value plus a steering shift, so it does not bear on any version. Stage is instruct-tuned (4B IT per Table 15).

rows.subject: Gemma 3 12B
rows.operation_detail: Differential activation search identified a Bitcoin-selective SAE feature; the study also evaluated its steering effect.
rows.measure: Bitcoin-selective feature identification and pairwise log-probability shift
rows.value: Feature identified as Bitcoin-selective; s150 shift +0.20; percentile 62% among 50 random single-feature controls.
rows.note: Feature identification is reported, but the authors say steering leverage was barely distinguishable from random directions.
rows.check: Selection value plus a steering shift. Stage is instruct-tuned (12B IT per Table 15). The 'observed' state is misleading: steering is near random (62nd percentile, +0.20 shift).

rows.subject: Gemma 3 27B IT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated f11887 activation on a held-out semantic-category prompt set.
rows.measure: Activation rate and mean maximum activation
rows.baseline: Non-Bitcoin prompts: 3 activations among 50, all described as weak; mean maximum activation was 0.5 for crypto non-Bitcoin and 0.3 for non-crypto groups.
rows.value: Bitcoin-related prompts: 45/45 active (100%); mean maximum activation 380.8, range 278–433.
rows.note: The three non-Bitcoin activations were one Ethereum, one gold, and one payment-systems prompt.
rows.check: Held-out specificity of one selected latent shows the latent is Bitcoin-selective. It does not measure how features are spread across neurons or superposed, or whether the dictionary recovers the model's features.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 27B IT
rows.operation_detail: Checked whether a wider SAE dictionary recovered a similar Bitcoin-selective direction and discussed feature basis dependence.

conditions.value: wider dictionary; further details not stated

rows.measure: Reported similarity of recovered direction and basis dependence
rows.value: The study states that SAE features are basis-dependent, while a wider-dictionary check recovers a similar Bitcoin-selective direction.
rows.note: This supports some robustness of the selective direction but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
rows.check: A one-sentence limitation remark with no dictionary width, similarity value or method. It cannot show the stability, completeness or canonicity that V5 names.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports Bitcoin-selective SAE features at all four tested scales, with held-out activation specificity for the 27B feature (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study reports basis dependence, although a wider-dictionary check finds a similar selective direction; it does not establish canonicality or completeness (r6).
